# The dependency set pyright sees in CI.
#
# This MUST stay a superset of the unit-test job's installs. `reportMissingImports`
# is `none`, so a package pyright cannot import becomes `Unknown` and stops
# constraining anything — which means a leaner environment is not a more
# permissive check, just a DIFFERENT one. Errors that appear only for some
# people are almost always this.
#
# The unit suite holds both halves: that every job running pyright installs from
# this file rather than inlining its own list, and that the `-r` chain below
# reaches every requirements file the test jobs install. Described rather than
# cited by path — a tree whose CI does not type-check is a configuration, not a
# defect, and this header must not name a file such a tree has deleted.
#
# ── This tree, which is one of the corners that header is written around ──
#
# It WAS such a tree until 2026-09-09: round 7 declined the template's job graph,
# so no workflow here ran pyright, and this file sat for six releases with no
# caller at all — configuration justified by a comment rather than by a caller.
# The operator ruled that CI should type-check, and the shape is a pyright STEP
# inside the existing `test` job rather than a job of its own, because a required
# check is named in branch protection and not discovered.
#
# That shape is what makes the three lines below the right ones. The template's
# type-check job installs this file onto the RUNNER's interpreter; this tree's
# pyright runs inside a job that has already built a `.venv`, and
# `pyrightconfig.json` pins `venvPath`/`venv` at it, so the interpreter pyright
# resolves is that venv. Every requirements file the venv installs therefore has
# to be reachable from here, or this file would declare a LEANER set than the one
# pyright actually reads — which is the differently-wrong check the header is
# about, with this file as the thing telling the lie.
#
# `tests/test_pyright_deps_reach_ci.py` is what holds it, because the template's
# own `tests/test_pyright_deps.py` is declined here and cannot run (it wants two
# test jobs; this tree has one pytest matrix). Named differently on purpose so
# that if the template's gate ever becomes satisfiable it arrives as a visible
# addition rather than silently overlapping this one. Keep one of the two.

-r ../requirements.txt
-r ../requirements-dev.txt
-r ../scripts/requirements.txt
